output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, time preference, as measured by savings behavior (DISSAVED and SAMESAVE), has a statistically significant positive relationship with BMI in Hispanic men. This suggests that individuals with a higher tendency to prioritize immediate rewards (as indicated by DISSAVED and SAMESAVE) are more likely to have higher BMI values. The statistical significance of this relationship is supported by p-values of 0 for both DISSAVED and SAMESAVE, indicating a strong and significant association.
